extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and instructors working through complex analysis problems (appendix of solution hints)
extracted.subtask_description: Hints and solution strategies for complex analysis exercise problems (contour integrals, analytic functions, singularity analysis, power/Laurent series, mapping properties, and related theorems). Intended to guide producing correct solutions and recognizing which theorems/techniques to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify complex differentiability via Cauchy–Riemann and partial derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that a function is complex differentiable at a point (or on a set) by showing its real and imaginary parts have appropriate first partial derivatives and satisfy the Cauchy–Riemann equations; continuity of first partials may be used (Proposition B.1 and related results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the decomposition f = u + iv, compute u_x,u_y,v_x,v_y, verify u_x = v_y and u_y = −v_x and the continuity hypotheses; for vector-valued/multiple-variable cases write Jacobian matrices and check the matrix equation equivalent to Cauchy–Riemann conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Cauchy Integral Formula to compute contour integrals and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Cauchy Integral Formula (and its corollaries) to evaluate integrals of analytic functions, compute derivatives at points inside a contour, and derive numeric integral values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parametrize the contour sensibly, isolate the contributing singular terms (or use residues), and when differentiating under the integral sign use Cauchy’s formula for derivatives (Corollary B.15/B.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametrize contours and reduce to standard integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Parametrize a given path (line segment, circle, straight line) appropriately so the integral reduces to a standard form or allows application of known theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: parametrize line segment by linear t, unit circle by z = e^{iθ}, choose parameter ranges so integrand simplifies; when integrating rational/trigonometric integrals, substitute z = e^{iθ} to convert to complex contour integral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Fubini’s Theorem for iterated integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting double integrals arising in contour integral manipulations, use Fubini’s Theorem to interchange order of integration and simplify expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure integrand measurability/absolute integrability conditions hold; once applied, use Cauchy–Riemann to show inner parentheses vanish if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Residue Theorem to evaluate integrals via poles
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute complex integrals by summing residues of integrand inside the contour and multiplying by 2πi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor denominator to identify poles, determine which poles lie inside the chosen contour (upper half-plane, unit disk, etc.), compute simple or higher-order residues via limits or Laurent coefficients, and add them. Use standard examples when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count zeros/poles using the Argument Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate integrals of f'/f around a closed curve to the number of zeros minus poles inside the curve (counting multiplicities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When f is nonvanishing on the contour, evaluate 1/(2πi)∮ f'(z)/f(z) dz to get the integer count; can be combined with Rouché’s theorem to compare numbers of zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rouché’s Theorem to compare zeros of analytic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: When one term dominates the sum on a contour, use Rouché’s Theorem to assert the two functions have the same number of zeros inside the contour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify dominating term (e.g., highest-degree polynomial term on large circle) and verify |g(z)| < |f(z)| on the contour; conclude f+g and f have same zero count inside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Maximum Modulus Theorem and its consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Maximum Modulus Theorem to deduce constancy, bounds, or uniqueness properties of analytic functions (e.g., when maxima are attained, or to bound 1/(z f(z))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with Liouville’s theorem or Schwarz’s Lemma in unit-disk settings; use to bound derivatives via Cauchy estimates when supremum on disk is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liouville’s Theorem for bounded entire functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude an entire function that is bounded in C is constant; use this to deduce further properties (e.g., constant must be particular value given asymptotics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a function is shown bounded everywhere (often via maximum modulus or limit relations), state Liouville’s conclusion and infer values required by extra constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity Theorem for analytic continuation and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Identity Theorem: if analytic functions agree on a set with a limit point in a region, they agree everywhere in the connected region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to deduce equality of entire functions given agreement on real or imaginary axis segments or sequences with accumulation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify isolated singularities (removable, pole, essential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the type of isolated singularity (removable/pole/essential) by examining Laurent series, behavior of f(1/z) at 0, or growth/limit properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cauchy’s estimates and Weierstrass theorem for essential singularities; for poles use order detection and Cauchy’s residue computations; for removable singularities, extend analytically and apply Liouville if whole-plane consequences follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass and Picard-type consequences for essential singularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage Weierstrass (or related) results: near an essential singularity the function attains values arbitrarily close to any complex number (used to construct sequences producing contradictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sequences approaching the singularity to force desired value behavior, often to show contradictions when global properties are assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy’s estimate to bound derivatives and deduce polynomial degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Cauchy’s estimate on disks to bound derivatives f^{(n)}(0) by M/r^n and conclude vanishing of high-order derivatives (hence polynomial degree bounds) when growth conditions are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose radii and use sup bound on disk; let parameters tend to infinity when required to force derivatives to zero beyond certain order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power series and Laurent series manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with Taylor and Laurent expansions to identify coefficients, parity properties, region-of-convergence annuli, and to compute residues or series expansions of composed/quotient functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract coefficients by matching expansions; when combining series use convolution/recurrence relations; pay attention to annuli for Laurent series validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use substitution z = e^{iθ} to transform real integrals to contour integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert real integrals (like ∫ f(cos θ) dθ) to complex contour integrals on unit circle via z = e^{iθ}, dz = i e^{iθ} dθ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify denominator roots, select the single root inside the unit disk if applicable, compute residue and translate back to original real integral value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascoli's Theorem and diagonal process for normal families
rubrics_metrics.description: To extract a subsequence converging uniformly on compacts from a sequence of equicontinuous, uniformly bounded functions on an increasing exhaustion of compacts, use Ascoli plus a diagonalization argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover the region by nested compacts Kn, pass to subsequences with uniform convergence on each Kn, then form diagonal subsequence that converges on every compact subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morera’s Theorem to deduce analyticity from vanishing integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuous function has integral zero over every closed piecewise C^1 curve in a region, then the function is analytic there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show uniform convergence of approximating integrands on compacts to pass limits under integrals; then apply Morera to the uniform limit to conclude analyticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform convergence on compacts preserves analyticity and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits of sequences of analytic functions that converge uniformly on compact subsets yield analytic limits; derivative convergence follows under uniform convergence of derivatives on compacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cauchy integral representations on small disks to deduce uniform convergence of derivatives from uniform convergence of functions on larger compact sets; apply in contradiction arguments (Argument Principle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use open mapping property of nonconstant analytic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonconstant analytic function maps open sets to open sets; use this to derive contradictions about boundary/value preimages or constancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with compactness arguments or properties of the image (e.g., contained in real axis) to deduce impossibility unless function is constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct harmonic conjugates by integrating CR equations on simply connected domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a harmonic function u on a simply connected region U whose first partials satisfy required conditions, construct a conjugate harmonic v by integrating (u_x,u_y) along polygonal paths parallel to axes and prove well-definedness by checking integral independence of path using contour arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix base point, define F by integrating iu2 and −iu1 along horizontal/vertical segments, use decomposition of loop into signed regions and Cauchy integrals to show path independence; then F is analytic with real part u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose holomorphic maps and compute Jacobians via real Jacobian product
rubrics_metrics.description: When composing holomorphic maps, compute real Jacobian matrices by multiplying the real Jacobians of components and show the composite satisfies the complex Jacobian matrix equation, hence is holomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chain rule for real-variable Jacobians, apply the matrix equation equivalence of CR conditions (Problem 4), and infer holomorphicity entrywise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect polynomial/rational nature by global growth and analytic continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a function is entire but has growth restrictions or is a quotient of polynomials with bounded denominator behavior, deduce that the function must be polynomial (or rational with specified degree) via fundamental theorem of algebra and boundedness arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show denominator cannot have roots (or that entire quotient is bounded), then conclude denominator constant and numerator polynomial; use limits at infinity and Cauchy estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute integrals by identifying and summing singular parts (partial fractions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Express rational functions as sums of singular parts at poles (partial fraction decomposition) and sum residues/singular parts to compute integrals or reconstruct original function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write P/Q as sum of principal parts at each pole plus entire function; match singular parts to deduce uniqueness; use residues to compute coefficients (ck = P(rk)/Q'(rk)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symmetry/parity and even/odd function properties in series
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit parity (even/odd) of numerator/denominator or function structure to simplify expansions (e.g., series in z^2) and to determine which coefficients vanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When function is quotient of odd functions or has explicit symmetry, infer only even or odd terms appear and compute coefficients accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose contours and radii carefully to place integration points in desired compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying Cauchy representations for derivatives or integrals, select contours of radius small enough that entire integrand and its approximants lie inside given compact sets (control distance to boundary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distance from compact K to complement of domain to pick radius d, then standard circle of radius ≤ d/2 about points in K stays inside domain and allows uniform estimates; apply to bound derivatives uniformly on K.
